subject: Anthropology
title: Explanatory Models
description: Learn Explanatory Models in one minute.

hook.text: A doctor says bacteria. A grandmother says the evil eye. A patient says stress. Everyone explains sickness differently.

buildup.text: Explanatory models are the beliefs patients hold about what caused their illness, what it means, and how to fix it.

discovery.text: Kleinman showed that doctors and patients often hold conflicting models, leading to miscommunication and poor care.

twist.text: Effective healing happens when doctors listen to the patient's model, not just impose their own biomedical one.

climax.text: Healing is negotiation. The best care bridges the gap between what the doctor knows and what the patient believes.

punchline.text: Good medicine starts with asking: what do you think caused this?

quiz.question: What are explanatory models?
options: Patient beliefs about what caused their illness and how to treat it

details.summary: Explanatory models are the frameworks people use to understand why they got sick, what their illness means, and what should be done about it. Patients' explanatory models often differ dramatically from biomedical explanations, causing clinical miscommunication.
details.whyItMatters: When a doctor says you have a bacterial infection and you believe illness comes from spiritual imbalance, treatment compliance suffers. Eliciting explanatory models bridges cultural gaps between patients and practitioners.
takeaways: Explanatory models are personal frameworks for understanding illness
Patients and doctors often hold fundamentally different models
Eliciting patient models improves communication and treatment outcomes

faq.question: What is Arthur Kleinman's explanatory model framework?
faq.answer: Kleinman proposed eight questions clinicians should ask patients: What do you call your problem? What caused it? Why did it start when it did? What does it do to your body? How severe is it? What do you fear? What treatment should you receive? These questions reveal the patient's framework.

faq.question: Why do patients and doctors often disagree about illness?
faq.answer: Doctors are trained in biomedical explanatory models emphasizing pathophysiology. Patients construct models from personal experience, cultural beliefs, and social context. A patient may attribute diabetes to emotional stress rather than metabolic dysfunction. Both perspectives have clinical value.
